title: Prefix-aware KV segmentation and liveness coordinator for multi-GPU caches
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: As we run continuous batching across heterogeneous multi-GPU pods, hot prefix patterns (short repeated token sequences at the start of requests) cause uneven KV cache pressure that reduces overall throughput and increases cross-GPU network traffic during pipeline/tensor parallel exchanges. Current slab/stripe strategies don't account for prefix locality or pipeline liveness windows, so hot prefixes either congest a single GPU or trigger excessive prefetch/eviction churn.
proposed_solution:
Introduce a prefix-aware segmentation layer and a liveness coordinator. Key ideas:
- Microsegments: split KV cache into small fixed-size microsegments (~256-1024 entries) aligned to token prefixes rather than contiguous KV offsets.
- HotPrefixAllocator: runtime component that tracks prefix hit-rate and assigns microsegments with high prefix affinity to GPUs based on pipeline liveness and current batch composition.
- Liveness windows: attach a short TTL and pipeline-liveness score to microsegments to prefer placement on GPUs that will be active for upcoming pipeline stages, reducing cross-device transfers.
- Background RebalanceDaemon: asynchronous mover that copies microsegments between GPUs during low-util periods using RDMA/peer-to-peer, with rate limits to avoid affecting SLOs.
- Continuous-batching integration: expose microsegment affinity hints to the batch planner so incoming requests are binned to pods where their prefix microsegments already reside when possible.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Increased metadata: microsegment map adds ~1-3% device memory overhead for hot-index tables.
- Rebalance cost: movers can consume PCIe bandwidth; must be throttled and coordinated with autoscaler.
- Consistency complexity: we maintain a single authoritative copy with write-through invalidation; risk of stale reads if rebalancer race occurs.
- Edge cases: extremely long-tail prefixes still require fallback to remote fetch path, potentially higher latency.
- Implementation complexity across tensor/pipeline parallel codepaths, interactions with KV spill-to-host and quantized memory layouts.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end correctness: no KV correctness regressions; unit tests for microsegment mapping and liveness eviction.
2) Perf target: reduce cross-GPU KV transfer volume by >=25% on the prefix-heavy benchmark (prefix-workload-v1) without increasing p50 generation latency by >5%.
3) Cost target: neutral or negative effect on average GPU memory due to slightly better packing of hot segments.
4) Observability: dashboards for microsegment placement, rebalance throughput, and prefix hit-rate exposed in Console.
5) Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag and enabled only for dedicated pods until validated.
test_plan:
- Simulated bench: run prefix-workload-v1 and a long-tail mixing workload across 16-pod heterogeneous cluster; compare baseline and feature-on metrics.
- Unit tests for allocator heuristics and liveness TTL expiration.
- Chaos tests: kill pods during background rebalance to validate correctness and fallback.
- Integration: validate batch planner affinity hints reduce cross-device fetch counts.
- Perf microbench: measure extra metadata overhead with large models (up to 70B).
implementation_steps:
1) Design doc and proto: prefix map schema, microsegment lifecycle (done). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Prefix+Microsegment+Design.
2) Runtime: implement HotPrefixAllocator component in serving runtime (step 1).
3) RebalanceDaemon: background mover with rate-limiting and backpressure hooks (step 2).
4) Batch planner changes: affinity hinting API and routing logic (step 3).
5) Telemetry: expose metrics and Console widgets (step 4).
6) QA and perf runs, canary rollout, iterate on heuristics (step 5).
rollout_plan:
- Feature flag behind runtime:prefix_microsegment_enabled.
- Canary: enable on 5 dedicated pods with mixed GPU types for 72h.
- Monitor: cross-GPU transfer rate, p50/p99 latency, Memory utilization, rebalance throttle metrics.
- Ramp: 25% pods -> 50% -> 100% dedicated over 2 weeks if targets met.
- Blocker criteria: >5% p99 latency regression, or Rebalance saturates PCIe > threshold for >10m.
monitoring_and_metrics: metrics: prefix_hit_rate, microsegment_locality_ratio, rebalance_bytes/sec, rebalance_ops, kb_transfer_saved, cache_eviction_rate, p50_gen_latency, p99_gen_latency, gpu_mem_overhead_pct.
open_questions:
- Optimal microsegment size across model scales (256 vs 1024 entries) — need A/B.
- Interaction with KV spill-to-host policy: should spilling prefer less-affine microsegments?
- Local vs authoritative copy model: currently plan single-authority with copy-on-write; evaluate multi-replica for extremely hot prefixes.
- How to represent prefix affinity for variable-length tokenization (BPE/spm) — use canonical normalized prefix sequences?
